title: Islamic Perspective on New Year Celebrations
summary: Hadith advises against adopting non-Islamic New Year customs.
translation: Today marks the end of our current year, and tomorrow the new year begins. In this context, it is important to understand that eagerly awaiting midnight and then congratulating each other, cutting cakes, or holding gatherings is not appropriate according to Islamic teachings, as these are practices of non-Muslims. Muslims should adhere to their traditions and follow their own religious teachings. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that whoever imitates a people, becomes one of them, and thus their fate will be similar. Therefore, one should avoid and abstain from such gatherings, and instead pray to Allah. This is a time for reflection: as a part of our life ends, another begins, reminding us that our life is fleeting. When we study the books of our predecessors, we learn that they made conscious efforts to perform good deeds every day. If they missed a day or were negligent, they regretted it. Abdullah ibn Masud (may Allah be pleased with him) said he regretted nothing more than a day where the sun set but he had not increased his good deeds. Similarly, Hassan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) stated that 'O son of Adam, you are but a collection of days; when a day passes, so does a part of you.' When we lose our belongings, we are either happy or sad; here, we lose parts of our life, yet we rejoice. Our death is approaching, our days and hours are decreasing. Hazrat Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said, 'These days are the scrolls of your life; fill them with good deeds.' If one does good deeds, that day will remain beneficial for his life and the hereafter, but if he does evil, the day will be considered wasted along with the punishment it brings. The best way is for a person to show the virtue of Islam by avoiding meaningless activities: 'One of the beautiful traits of Islam is that a person avoids what does not concern them.' Celebrating with New Year’s parades and greetings or saying phrases like 'Happy New Year' is not appropriate according to Shariah. A person should reflect on past time and prepare a plan for future success in both life and the hereafter.
